definitions.explanation: lacking fairness or justice, especially in how people or situations are treated

examples.japanese: {不公正|ふこうせい}な{取引|とりひき}だ。
{不公正|ふこうせい}な{扱|あつか}いに{抗議|こうぎ}した。
examples.english: I protested against the unjust treatment.

examples.japanese: {社会|しゃかい}の{不公正|ふこうせい}を{正|ただ}すために{活動|かつどう}している{団体|だんたい}がある。
examples.english: There are organizations working to correct social injustice.

notes:
Composed of {不|ふ} (non-/un-) and {公正|こうせい} (fairness/justice). Used as both a na-adjective ({不公正|ふこうせい}な) and a noun ({不公正|ふこうせい}). Common in formal discussions about social issues, legal matters, and business practices.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不公正|ふこうせい}な{取引|とりひき}: unfair transaction
- {不公正|ふこうせい}な{扱|あつか}い: unjust treatment
- {不公正|ふこうせい}を{正|ただ}す: to correct injustice
- {社会|しゃかい}の{不公正|ふこうせい}: social injustice

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {不公平|ふこうへい}: unfair — focuses on unequal distribution or treatment between people
- {不当|ふとう}: unjust, unreasonable — broader, can mean inappropriate or undeserved
- {不正|ふせい}: dishonest, fraudulent — implies deliberate wrongdoing or corruption
